The Chicago Cubs were one of the original baseball teams going back to the late 1800's. They were very good at the turn of the century (1900's) and won a few World Series titles during that decade. Their last World Series (WS) win was in 1908. They did make a WS appearance in 1945 but lost. Then there was also the "curse of the billy goat" thing that you can do an internet search on if you want. For the next many years the Cubs were a laughingstock to most baseball fans. They would get to the precipice of winning their division only to fail miserably like in 1969 when they dropped a huge lead going into September and the NY Mets took the division championship and eventually the WS. Huge stretches of time would go by when the Cubs were just awful, with no hope of winning anything. Basement dwellers in their division year after year. They had a good team in the 80's for a couple of years and came within one win of advancing to the WS but lost three in a row to the San Diego Padres and failed yet again.

Another couple decades of failure goes by. They did have some good teams and good players but it was all for naught and the ridicule continued. The Loveable Losers. Still their fan base was very loyal as their home venue, Wrigley Field, is an iconic baseball park and a super fun place to go see a game (the entire place is surrounded by bars and restaurants and vendors) and you can get there super easy by taking the train. There's no parking really so that's what everyone does. There was a "Bartman" series in the early 2000's that yet again the Cubs failed, it was pretty famous for being yet another example of the "curse of the billy goat".

Then in 2016 they had a great team and won their division, and then won the NCLS which means they were going to the WS for the first time since 1945. Their opponent was the Cleveland Indians, another team who had a very long drought. Both teams have super loyal fan bases. The WS is a best of seven series. Win 4 out of 7 and you win. The Cubs quickly fell to 1-3, and the media was howling their derision. Cubs fans always believe there's a chance though. Cardinals fans, the Cubs bitter division rivals, were mercilessly mocking Cubs fans (believe me) and then the Cubs won two games in dramatic fashion. Now it was tied 3-3 and the last game went back to Cleveland. Home field advantage to them. Cubs fans were basically all installing heart pacemakers at this point. Then the Cubs came out quickly and took a commanding lead. Our starting pitcher was superb! Then, all the sudden, late in the game the Indians scored a bunch of runs and it looked yet again like Cubs were going to lose. And to top it off, it started to rain so hard they had an hour-long rain delay where the Cubs could stew in their own juices.

After the rain delay most Cubs fans were so freaking nervous it was nuts. It was the top of the 9th for the Cubs, they had to score or it was over. And with two outs they scored the tying run, then held the Indians in the bottom of the 9th to force extra innings. Runs were traded back and forth, it was so nerve wracking at the time. Then the Cubs scored in the 11th, and held the Indians just enough to pull off the win and win their first WS title in 108 years. They said it couldn't be done, but they did it. This was right during the 2016 election and with both a Cubs win and Trump winning, it was a great time to be alive if you were a Cubs/Trump fan.
